plan.title: Adipose treated vs control: variance partition + DE
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human adipose bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated vs 6 control, Salmon-derived gene counts, 12000 genes) with sex and age recorded per sample, single batch, unpaired. The research question has two parts. Part 1: before testing the treated-vs-control contrast, quantify how much of the per-gene expression variance is explained by condition, sex, and age individually — this is a variancePartition diagnostic, not a hypothesis test, and it informs whether sex/age must be modeled as covariates (which the metadata already tells us they should be, per design best practice with n=6/group). Part 2: the DE test itself uses DESeq2 with condition, sex, and age all in the design formula (age as a fixed continuous covariate, centered), Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH-FDR at 0.05, followed by fgsea preranked enrichment on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome + WikiPathways (follow-up), all present in the reference store for human. QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) precedes both. With only 6 per group, DESeq2's Cook's-distance NA-flagging behavior applies and must be reported; the enrichment step must not fall back to an over-representation test since the significant gene count is expected to be small at this replicate depth. Strandedness is unknown for these Salmon-quantified counts; since only gene-level counts (not quant.sf) are provided, we cannot re-run strand inference from alignments — this is noted as a caveat on the counts as delivered rather than a blocking gap, since the counts are already gene-summarized and salmon-quantified upstream.
